newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mass murderer swears lawyer to silence on motive.
newsitem.headline: Mass murderer swears lawyer to silence on motive.

text.p: Australian mass killer Martin Bryant has revealed to his lawyer the motive for his slaughter of 35 people at Port Arthur last April, but has asked it remain a secret, his lawyer John Avery said on Thursday.

"He knows fully why he did it and what he did and he has disclosed that to me," Avery said a radio interview aired on Thursday. "I am not at liberty to divulge that of course without his express instructions..."

Bryant, who has confessed to the April 28 murders at a tourist spot in the southern island state of Tasmania, is awaiting sentencing on Friday after a chilling two-day sentencing hearing which ended here on Wednesday.

The Tasmanian Supreme Court, packed with distraught family of the victims and massacre survivors, heard how Bryant planned the killings weeks and perhaps months before he unleashed the shooting spree at Port Arthur.
The site, strewn with the ruins of an old penal colony, was crowded with tourists when Bryant suddenly opened fire on a fine autumn afternoon with two military-style firearms.

Both Avery and prosecutor Damian Bugg agree Bryant was not criminally insane but suffered a rare personality disorder, Asperger's Syndrome, and severely limited intelligence. But he knew the difference between right and wrong, the court heard.
As long ago as 1991, a psychiatrist who examined the desperate loner wrote: "...he continually threatens violence. Martin tells me he would like to go around shooting people".
Bryant, 29, was on Thursday back in his isolation, maximum-security prison cell where, his lawyer had told the court, he accepted he would spend the rest of his life.
"He specifically instructed me to put to the court what I did and that was, in this instance, that he never be released from prison," Avery said after the hearing ended on Wednesday.
"He understands what that means," Avery told reporters.
